name: Sticky Lab
summary: Workbench: measure what your Sticky can do – refresh, dithering, touch, sensors, energy, pins and restarts – plus a hidden game.
description: Eleven stations that probe the reTerminal Sticky and its 3.97-inch e-ink: refresh types and ghosting with timings, fonts with magnifier, six dithering methods, Braun-style controls, animation frame rates, touch accuracy and latency, gauges for climate, level, clock and battery, energy per refresh and in sleep, an on-screen keyboard with typing speed, and a pins & restarts diagnosis that makes a crash loop visible on the device (pin levels and interrupts, reset reasons, interrupt-storm detector). Plus a hidden castle-duel game. Logs to /lab/messungen.csv on the microSD. English and German. The browser Sticky Console mirrors and remote-controls the device.

compatibility.notes: microSD optional (measurements and screenshots go to /lab/). Works with both display controllers (SSD1677/SSD2677). Leaves data of other firmwares in flash and on the card alone.

assets.previewAlt: reTerminal Sticky running Sticky Lab: the same lit sphere dithered four ways on e-paper

notes.title: Back up the factory firmware first
notes.description: It contains device-specific data: esptool read-flash 0 0x2000000 backup.bin. Restore with write-flash 0 backup.bin.

notes.title: Controls
notes.description: AI short = overview, AI hold = screenshot to microSD, ▲/▼ = page or choose, tap = action, tap the status line = help. On the overview ▲ switches English/German.

notes.title: Sticky Console
notes.description: Open https://markussstaub-dot.github.io/sticky-lab/console/ in Edge or Chrome and connect over USB: mirror at actual size, remote control, measurements and a live tech inventory.
